fields.explanation: E.A and E.B are the numbers 1 and 2 at runtime, so + adds them and the result is 3. The names A and B do survive on the emitted enum object, as keys and as values in its reverse mapping (E[1] is "A"), but + only ever sees the numbers, so neither "AB" nor 12 from string concatenation can happen. Adding two numeric enum members is also not a type error.

fields.explanation: Y auto-numbers to 1 (X is 0), and because C is a const enum the compiler replaces C.Y with that value: the output is console.log(1 /* C.Y */); and no C object exists at runtime. A plain enum would emit an object and keep the C.Y lookup, and so does a const enum compiled with isolatedModules, which is why the question fixes the flags. That inlining is also why const enums are avoided in shared code: a mismatched dependency version can bake in stale values.
